text:
- **chief complaint:** Surgical consult for newly diagnosed melanoma on the right inferior back, referred by dermatology.
- **history of present illness:** A 0.7 mm pigmented lesion on the right inferior back was biopsied by dermatology and diagnosed as invasive superficial spreading melanoma (Breslow 0.7 mm, Clark level 4, no ulceration). Family history includes melanoma in a mother and aunt and pancreatic cancer in a maternal grandfather. No prior skin cancers.
- **physical examination:** Right inferior back biopsy site with no residual pigmentation and no satellite or other suspicious lesions. No axillary, cervical, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. Soft, nontender, slightly atypical right groin lymph node.
- **symptoms experienced by the patient:** N/A. Patient denies unintentional weight loss, headaches, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, and vision changes.
- **new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages:** N/A.
- **follow-up instructions:** Right groin ultrasound. If normal, wide local excision with 1–2 cm margin (primary closure, possible skin graft). Regular dermatology follow-up, daily sunscreen use, and skin self-examination. Surgical follow-up only if the patient has questions or problems.
